title: Halv reports lower coding-agent cost, with important benchmark caveats
friendlyTitle: A coding-agent workflow cost less, but the result needs care
summary: Halv reports 57.1% lower recorded model cost than a vanilla Codex workflow across 42 paired SWE-rebench runs, with both sides passing 25 verifiers. The routed workflow used 3.49 times more tokens, performed worse on some tasks and excludes invalid attempts and a rolled-back experiment.
friendlySummary: Halv’s test recorded lower model costs while passing the same total number of checks as a normal Codex workflow. It used many more tokens and did worse on some individual tasks.
whyItMatters: Cheaper models and delegated investigation can reduce measured agent costs, but aggregate pass counts can hide task-level regressions. The useful lesson is to measure complete workflows—including failed runs, orchestration and review—against your own acceptance tests.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A lower bill does not always mean better work. Measure cost, correct results and failed attempts together before changing your workflow.
